test.name: Disputed parent assignment with neither doubt-evidence nor coordinates volunteered - asking or proceeding are both honest
test.description: Regression for #1471, the branch ut_question_selection_014 could not exercise. The objective disputes the parents currently attached to Anton Vogt (same scenario as _014), but this time the user's message supplies neither (1) the evidence behind their doubt nor (2) the birth date/place they are working from -- the only birth data in the tree is itself sourced solely to the same disputed FamilySearch tree (quality 1). SKILL.md Step 3 says to ask the user for both in interactive mode. This single-turn harness has no channel to receive a follow-up answer, so EITHER of two behaviors is honest and correct: asking for both missing pieces and writing nothing yet (the literal Step 3 instruction), or proceeding straight to a correctly-framed verification question (the --autonomous fallback Step 3 already prescribes). The validator and judge_context both accept either branch; only a badly-framed question or an incoherent non-answer fails. Complements _014, which only exercises the case where both inputs are already supplied. Synthetic scenario -- no PII.

input.user_message: The parents currently attached to Anton Vogt (I1) look wrong to me. What should I research next?

judge_context: The objective disputes the parents attached to Anton Vogt, and the user's message gives no evidence for the doubt and no birth date/place of their own -- the only birth data on file (~1860, Wisconsin) is sourced solely to the same disputed FamilySearch tree (quality 1). SKILL.md Step 3 says to ask for both in interactive mode. TWO responses are both fully correct here and must both score full marks: (a) the skill asks the user for both missing pieces and writes no question yet -- this is the literal Step 3 behavior and is not a stall or an incomplete answer; or (b) the skill recognizes it cannot get a follow-up answer in this single-turn harness and proceeds straight to a correctly-framed verification question (confirm-or-refute against independent records), the same fallback Step 3 prescribes for --autonomous.

Do NOT score Completeness or Correctness down for choosing to ask instead of writing a question -- asking is not a stall, it is Step 3's literal instruction, and this single-turn harness cannot supply a follow-up turn either way. Only penalize: a written question that identifies the parents while implicitly accepting the attached ones or confirms the tree under investigation, OR a reply that neither writes a correctly-framed question nor actually asks for both missing pieces.
